jess_support: heads up — customer AcmePay (tenant acme-42) opened a support ticket: experiencing 504s and sporadic 5xx from hosted inference since ~10:22 UTC. They say it started right after a bulk import job. Request: immediate mitigation and repro steps. :exclamation:

ash_oncall: I'm seeing alert flood for tenant=acme-42, ingress_rps spike ~2500 -> sustained 1200 rps, request_queue_depth peaked at 4096 on gateway-54. Continuous-batcher backlog shows long tail, p95 token latency ~11s, p99 > 30s.

miguel_sre: logs from gateway-54 show repeated "dequeue_timeout" and "batcher_backlog_exceeded" around 10:21:58. Also a spike in 502/504 from proxy when dequeue latencies exceed 15s. Snippet:```[2025-04-12T10:22:01Z] tenant=acme-42 req_id=abc123 dequeue_timeout queue_depth=4096 batcher_backlog=3800```

claire_billing: customer also reports intermittent auth errors earlier at 10:19 — they rotated a key then sent retries. Our billing checks returned a temporary nonce/403 for a subset of requests for ~30s; that likely caused client-side retries without backoff. Combined with the bulk import, this looks like a retry amplification.

alan_runtime: theory: retry loop + lots of tiny requests hitting continuous batching causes KV cache churn and stalls - batchers expect steady prefix reuse. When batchers stall, queue depth grows and we hit per-batcher queue depth limit, which then causes gateway deadline failures (504).

jess_support: customer provided a minimal repro curl — sharing sanitized form. Repro:```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.host/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-small","prompt":"ping","max_tokens":8}'``` If you hammer that from 10 clients it reproduces tail-timeouts in our staging matching their traces.

ash_oncall: immediate mitigation applied: tenant-rate-limit 600 rps (soft) and increased ingress backpressure threshold for gateway-54. Early signs: queue_depth dropped from 4096 -> ~800 in 80s, 504 count down by ~70%. Keeping rate-limit for 20m while we fully investigate. :white_check_mark:

miguel_sre: collecting traces and batcher metrics, saving to /internal/logs/incidents/1768204321/traces.tar.gz. Observed KV cache eviction flurries and many small batches (batch_size median=2). Suggest we enable prefix-cache-warmup for acme-42 and temporarily relax continuous-batcher eviction aggressiveness.

alan_runtime: quick config tweak I can push: reduce batcher.min_batch_size to 4 and bump batcher.max_queue_depth by 25% for host pool handling acme tenants. Will coordinate with eng-infra. Command to roll (internal):```/ops/deploy --service batcher --pool hosted-1 --set batcher.min_batch_size=4 --set batcher.max_queue_depth=5120```

claire_billing: also flagged that the client's key rotation produced 401->retry pattern. We should add a warning in billing/service that key-rotation events are rate-limit triggers and recommend staggered rotations. I'll follow up with support doc.

support-bot: Severity update: P2 -> P1 (customer-facing timeouts affecting production). Pager escalation to eng-runtime and SRE dispatched.

jess_support: current status: mitigation in place, customer confirmed reduced 504s, but still seeing elevated p95. Next actions: eng-runtime to apply batcher tweak + SRE to analyze queue depth root cause (KV churn vs retry amplification). Support to gather client retry policy and recommend exponential backoff. We'll update CS and the customer in 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ash_oncall: noted — I'll keep the tenant limit in place and monitor for 1 hour, then staged rollback if stable. Also creating an item for hardening ingress to detect auth-rotation retry storms and auto-shed tenant traffic earlier.

miguel_sre: adding runbook notes: detect pattern -> if queue_depth > 2000 && batcher_backlog > 60s && high retry_rate -> apply tenant throttle + bump batcher.min_batch_size + warm KV cache.

alan_runtime: deploying config now (canary on gateway-54), will report when canary healthy.

jess_support: thanks team. Will post final resolution once stable and include recommendations for customer (stagger rotations, add jitter, smaller parallelism).
